title: TNFR2 stimulation induces pathological T-cell activation in a Parkinson’s disease mouse model
title_zh: TNFR2刺激在帕金森病小鼠模型中诱导病理性T细胞激活
abstract: Abstract Dysregulated T-cell responses and neuroinflammation are key contributors to neurodegeneration in Parkinson’s disease (PD). Modulation of regulatory T-cells (Tregs) to restore immune balance has therefore emerged as a potential neuroprotective strategy. In this study, we investigated whether systemic treatment with the tumor necrosis factor receptor type 2 (TNFR2) agonist NewSTAR2 enhances Treg function and mitigates neuroinflammation in a PD mouse model. We found that PD-derived Tregs maintain an intrinsic capacity to respond to TNFR2 stimulation, exhibiting increased activation and suppressive function. However, NewSTAR2 concurrently activated the pro-inflammatory immune compartment in the PD environment, thereby possibly counteracting potential neuroprotective effects. These findings suggest that PD-associated immune alterations redirect the overall response to TNFR2 stimulation away from a regulatory phenotype. Collectively, our results refine the current knowledge on immune dysregulation in PD and underscore the importance of disease context in the development of TNFR2-targeting therapies.
abstract_zh: 摘要 帕金森病（PD）中失调的T细胞反应和神经炎症是神经退行性变的关键促成因素。因此，通过调节调节性T细胞（Tregs）来恢复免疫平衡已成为一种潜在的神经保护策略。在本研究中，我们调查了系统给药促TNFR2受体（TNFR2）激动剂NewSTAR2是否能增强Treg功能并缓解PD小鼠模型中的神经炎症。我们发现，PD来源的Tregs保留了对TNFR2刺激的内在能力，表现出增强的激活和抑制功能。然而，NewSTAR2同时也激活了PD环境中的炎性免疫细胞群，从而可能抵消潜在的神经保护作用。这些发现表明，PD相关的免疫改变将对TNFR2刺激的整体反应偏离监管表型。综上所述，我们的结果完善了PD中免疫失调的当前认识，并强调了疾病背景在TNFR2靶向治疗开发中的重要性。
